- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after a price spike (e.g., 85+), then corrects downward — apply a “cool-down” factor: reduce forecast by 2–5% after peak.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust — anticipate downward correction and reduce forecast slope.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.67/0.33), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast curve, avoid sharp turns.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 75% of forecast’s 1st day value, model is overconfident — reduce initial forecast by 3–5%.
